methodological_rigor.justification: Multicenter, 22-site randomized phase II trial with 1:1 allocation stratified by macrovascular invasion, prior TKI, and prior TACE count, and dynamic randomization by independent third party. ITT for efficacy and as-treated for safety were prespecified with a valid sample-size calculation (84 per arm + 10% dropout for HR 0.65). The principal limitation is open-label design with local investigator adjudication of response rather than blinded independent central review, acknowledged by the authors, and the composite primary endpoint introduces investigator discretion particularly around TACE failure/refractoriness. Sensitivity analyses (mRECIST, RECIST 1.1, subgroups, post hoc exclusion of prior therapy) were performed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual randomized controlled trial (phase II), which maps to Oxford LoE 1b. The 7.6-month PFS improvement (HR 0.34) and 66% progression risk reduction in unresectable HCC including CNLC IIIa patients with Vp3-4 thrombus—populations excluded from EMERALD-1 and LEAP-012—are clinically relevant and fill a real evidence gap. OS is not yet mature and toxicity (74% grade >=3 TRAE, 3% treatment-related deaths) tempers immediate practice adoption.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript aligns well with CONSORT: CONSORT diagram (Fig 1), randomization/stratification described, eligibility, endpoints prespecified, subgroup analyses labeled post hoc, safety detailed, and limitations discussed. The trial registration identifier is not visible in the normalized text (only protocol acronym CHANCE2005/CARES-005), and there is no explicit data-sharing statement or repository; protocol and appendices are referenced but availability details are absent from the main text. Adverse event and crossover reporting are thorough.

novelty_literature.justification: The triplet concept (TACE + ICI + VEGFR TKI) is contemporaneous with several completed or ongoing trials (EMERALD-1, LEAP-012, TALENTACE) cited in the manuscript, so the combination itself is not first-in-class. Novelty comes from enriching for CNLC IIIa/Vp3-4 populations excluded elsewhere, use of RECICL 5 composite endpoint, and the specific camrelizumab+rivoceranib backbone from CARES-310. This represents a meaningful extension of prior work rather than a paradigm shift.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized into IMRaD sections with well-defined eligibility, endpoints, and statistical framework. Comparisons to EMERALD-1, LEAP-012 and TALENTACE are cogently discussed, and limitations are stated explicitly. Figures are descriptive and numerical reporting (CIs, HRs, percentages) is consistent. Some operational details (masking, ICR) are relegated to appendices, limiting main-text completeness.

key_strengths: Multicenter randomized phase II with dynamic stratified allocation and prespecified ITT analysis
Large, clinically meaningful PFS benefit (10.8 vs 3.2 months, HR 0.34) with consistent results across mRECIST and subgroups
Includes CNLC IIIa/Vp3-4 thrombus population that was excluded from EMERALD-1, LEAP-012, and TALENTACE
Thorough safety reporting including immune-related AEs and treatment-related deaths
key_concerns: Open-label design without blinded independent central review introduces assessment bias for composite endpoint
Composite PFS endpoint with TACE failure/refractoriness criteria allows investigator discretion that may inflate between-arm difference
Population restricted to Chinese, mostly HBV-related HCC; generalizability untested
OS immature (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.57-1.32) and heavy crossover (75%) limits ability to assess survival benefit
High grade >=3 TRAE rate (74%) and three treatment-related deaths in TACE-C-R arm
No explicit data-sharing statement or trial registration ID visible in normalized text
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-executed multicenter phase II RCT in a high-burden HCC subpopulation with a large PFS effect, but open-label design, composite endpoint discretion, immature OS, and substantial toxicity keep the manuscript just short of top-tier practice-changing status; tier 1 is plausible with minor revisions strengthening reporting and prespecified OS analysis.
